retrieval_text: A 76-year-old Caucasian woman presented with a 3-year history of a recurrent itchy rash on the hips, thighs, and under the breasts, accompanied by intermittent lesions resembling vesicles and bullae. Previous treatments with topical and intralesional corticosteroids provided minimal relief. The patient also experienced swelling in the lower extremities. She had a history of long-standing severe lichen sclerosis et atrophicus. Several months before the onset of the rash, she underwent radical vulvectomy and bilateral inguino-femoral lymph node dissection for stage 2/grade 2 invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva. Physical examination revealed multiple erosions with hemorrhagic crusts and multiple clustered translucent papules on the inframammary breasts, abdomen, hips, and proximal thighs. Both legs exhibited 4+ pitting and nonpitting edema along with scattered small vesicular lesions.

An eight-month-old female infant, born at term to non-consanguineous parents, presented with multiple hypopigmented skin lesions on the trunk and extremities since birth. Initially, these appeared as linear erosions that healed within a few days, leaving behind hypopigmentation with hyperpigmented borders. The perinatal period was uneventful. Limb and nail abnormalities were noted from birth, and developmental milestones were delayed. The patient had a history of exomphalos minor, which was surgically corrected, and an atrial septal defect that closed spontaneously by three months of age. No similar symptoms were reported in siblings or other family members. General examination showed microcephaly, hypertelorism, megalopinna, low-set ears, a broad nasal bridge, and a pointed chin. Skin examination revealed multiple hypopigmented atrophic linear streaks and macules of varying sizes on the forehead, neck, trunk, thighs, gluteal region, genitalia, and upper and lower limbs, following the lines of Blaschko. There was syndactyly of the left foot and ectrodactyly (lobster claw deformity) of the right foot. The patient had supernumerary nipples and a few skin-colored growths over the proximal nail fold of the right middle finger and right foot. Nails were dystrophic, while hair and oral mucosa were normal. Systemic examination was unremarkable.

A 23-year-old male presented with breathing difficulties and weight loss persisting for 8 months. Dermatology consultation was requested for skin lesions. Physical examination revealed pallor and enlarged submandibular and occipital lymph nodes. Skin examination identified multiple erythematous papules and nodules on the trunk, face, and scalp, with ulceration and scarring in both axillae. Some lesions had central umbilication and others were covered with adherent scales. Bronchial breath sounds were noted over the lower chest bilaterally with occasional crepitations. Peripheral blood smear showed normocytic normochromic red blood cells, neutrophilic leucocytosis, and relative lymphopenia, with no atypical cells or blasts. Hemoglobin was 8.5 gm/dL, erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 37 mm/hour, C-reactive protein was 10.

A 69-year-old Caucasian woman reported new visual disturbances in her left eye, which began approximately ten weeks prior to her visit to the uveitis clinic in March 2023. She experienced new floaters and central flashing initially, followed by the development of an enlarging scotoma and progressive vision loss about four weeks later. Four weeks before the onset of these ocular symptoms, she tested positive for COVID-19 antibodies and experienced fever, congestion, and cough. She had received the COVID-19 vaccination several months before contracting the infection. Her medical history includes asthma, hypothyroidism, and headaches. There is no notable family history or prior autoimmune disease.

A seven-month-old male child presented with asymmetry in the size of the eyes, with the left eye being smaller than the right. He was born at full term to parents who are first cousins, following an uneventful pregnancy and normal vaginal delivery. Ocular examination revealed a smaller left eyelid, and upon retracting the eyelids, the socket was found to be empty. The right eye appeared normal. Systemic examination identified multiple congenital anomalies, including a head circumference of 34 cm (below the third percentile for his age), abnormalities in the external ear and fingers, hydrocele, and hypospadias. The left ear was malformed with hypoplasia of the antihelices, fusion of the helix with the tragus, and an obscured external auditory canal opening. The left hand had four normal digits and a pre-axial duplication of the thumb, while the right hand was normal. The child was unable to sit with support, potentially due to kyphosis of the thoracic vertebral column. Dental abnormalities and cognitive impairment could not be excluded.

An 18-year-old male presented with multiple painless skin swellings located on the right cheek, chin, eyelid, and suprapubic region. The swelling on the right cheek had been recurring for 4 years. The patient had a history of recurrent cardiac swellings in the left atrium and right ventricle, for which he had undergone surgery twice. He also experienced a cerebrovascular accident. There was no notable family history. On physical examination, the swelling on the right cheek measured 15 x 8 x 6 cm, was firm, non-tender, mobile, and not attached to underlying structures. The overlying skin was nodular and had areas of ulceration. The swellings on the right eyelid, chin, and suprapubic region measured 0.5 cm, 2.0 cm, and 3.5 cm, respectively. Additionally, there was a small pigmented lesion on the inner canthus of the right eye, multiple pigmented macules on the left shin, and several nevi on the legs and back. The patient also had vitiligo on the prepuce. Endocrine evaluation showed elevated adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) levels at 48.5 pg/mL.

A 36-year-old male with bilateral sensorineural hearing loss was referred to the Department of Radiology. He is the first of two brothers born to healthy parents of Turkish descent, who are first cousins. The younger brother is healthy. There is no other family history of deafness in the extended family. At the age of 9 months, the hearing impairment was noticed. An audiologic assessment confirmed severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, and the loss was corrected with a hearing aid. Hearing loss has remained stable. He had no school problems and graduated from high school. On physical examination, he has no dysmorphic features. He has neither an obvious neurological difficulty nor a cognitive impairment.

A 4-day-old full-term male infant, born to a 19-year-old mother, was admitted to the neonatal ICU due to bilious vomiting and delayed passage of meconium. Physical examination revealed discoloration of the forehead hair, eyes, and right forearm.

A 24-year-old male reported experiencing an itchy, softened plaque primarily located in the left perineal area, which has been present since he was 5 years old and has shown periods of worsening and improvement. The affected area extends from the perineal region to the scrotum and the inner part of the left thigh. A comprehensive examination did not reveal any other abnormalities in the body. There was no notable family history.

A 37-year-old woman reported experiencing pain in her right leg for six months and in her left leg for four weeks. The pain in the left leg was mild, whereas the pain in the right leg had progressively worsened.

A 57-year-old Hispanic male presented for retinal evaluation due to a progressive decline in central vision in both eyes over 7 months, more pronounced in the right eye. He reported difficulty reading, watching TV, and experiencing bilateral light sensitivity. He denied any new visual distortions, floaters, flashing lights, head or eye trauma, prior eye surgeries, or a history of strabismus or amblyopia. His ophthalmic history was notable only for poor night vision since childhood. Family history was negative for retinal diseases, and his children and grandchildren reported no night vision issues. His general medical history included well-controlled hypertension managed with lisinopril.

A 48-year-old woman reported experiencing floaters, flashes of light, blurred vision, and eye pain in both eyes for several days before her visit. She had a 10-year history of diabetes mellitus and was on glibenclamide and metformin.

A 30-year-old obese Caucasian female presented to the emergency department with fatigue persisting for three months. She reported recent episodes of dizziness, lightheadedness, and shortness of breath during physical activity. Additionally, she experienced diffuse, relapsing-remitting lower abdominal pain over the same period.
A 64-year-old Caucasian woman presented with ulcers on both sides of her lower legs, which had been present for approximately 1 year and developed without any external trauma.

A 16-year-old female patient exhibited a 10.5 × 8.0 cm grayish-depressed plaque with hypochromic areas on the lower half of her left thigh lateral. Telangiectatic vessels were observed around the periphery of the lesion, with visible veins nearby. The plaque has been present since birth, initially appearing violet and gradually becoming whitened and depressed over time. There is no difference in the length of the lower limbs.

A one-year-old girl was brought to our center due to delays in neurodevelopment, bilateral hearing loss, and visual issues. Her parents are first cousins. The perinatal history was without complications. Physical examination showed normal growth parameters. She had bilateral hearing loss and was using hearing aids. The liver was palpable 6 cm below the right costal margin. Notable facial features included arched eyebrows, a broad nasal root, low set ears, downward slanting eyes, epicanthal folds, strabismus, and a myopathic face.
A 51-year-old male presented with several months of progressively worsening headaches, visual disturbances, and gait imbalance. Physical examination revealed papilledema and poor tandem gait.
A 49-year-old female patient presented with numbness in her fingers that gradually extended to her entire body above the bellybutton over a period of six months.
A 42-year-old Caucasian male presented with a history of progressive fatigue, chills, night sweats, and unintended weight loss. Physical examination revealed left cervical lymphadenopathy.

A 63-year-old Caucasian female with a history of diabetes mellitus reported a progressively enlarging cutaneous nodule in the lower mid-back region. She did not experience trauma, skin discharge, weight loss, fever, or night chills but did report mild fatigue.
